description.value: A sham-controlled study assessing the effects of high-frequency right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex rTMS on emotion processing, emotion reappraisal, craving, and related BOLD activity in alcohol use disorder patients and healthy controls.

spans.text: The current study is the first to investigate the effect of high-frequency rTMS on emotion processing and reappraisal in AUD patients and HCs at a behavioral and neural level.

value: we hypothesize that high-frequency rTMS of the right dlPFC ameliorates reappraisal and the recruitment of the reappraisal-related brain network in both AUD patients and HCs, but this improvement is expected to be greater in the AUD group compared to the HC group
We expect that high-frequency stimulation will influence (increase or decrease) emotion processing at a behavioral and neural level.
Finally, we expect that in AUD patients, high-frequency stimulation decreases reappraisal task-induced craving.

spans.text: Based on previous studies ( 29 ), we hypothesize that high-frequency rTMS of the right dlPFC ameliorates reappraisal and the recruitment of the reappraisal-related brain network in both AUD patients and HCs, but this improvement is expected to be greater in the AUD group compared to the HC group

value: Although none of the two-way interactions reached significance, there was a trend-significant interaction between image type and stimulation. This interaction originated from a difference in the effect of rTMS on brain activity between the reappraisal of positive and negative images in the bilateral superior frontal gyrus for both AUD patients and HCs: rTMS decreased superior frontal gyrus activity during reappraisal of negative images and increased activity during reappraisal of positive images relative to sham stimulation.
